personas.caption: Six role lenses, written as jobs to be done. Authored for testing; not validated biographies. Source: U02 research synthesis.

roles.job: When a practical is unfamiliar, identify the method, complete kit and next action so I can begin with an understood question.
roles.outcome: First preparation → explain the task and readiness requirements
roles.check: Previous familiarity, how preparation happens, acceptable help and real stopping points

roles.job: When conditions change, reconstruct and compare what I actually recorded so I can defend a bounded interpretation.
roles.outcome: Variation, failed capture or later report → trace evidence without rewriting history
roles.check: Current notebook habits, significance of parameter differences, preferred comparison depth

roles.job: When preparing or teaching a cohort, distinguish readiness from learning so I can offer the right support.
roles.outcome: Upcoming practical or confusing evidence → a support action, not a completion ranking
roles.check: Assessment expectations, attendance ownership, what readiness signals actually mean

roles.job: When an asset fails or a kit returns incomplete, establish impact and ownership so the next user has a reliable status.
roles.outcome: Incident or handover → restriction, repair verification and clear next action
roles.check: Existing SOPs, notification responsibility, inventory accuracy and release authority

roles.job: When reviewing demand and resources, reconcile definitions and scope so I can make a documented decision.
roles.outcome: Planning review → qualified utilisation and resource evidence
roles.check: Real reporting period, permitted data, baseline and denominators

roles.job: When finding the lab or an activity, obtain useful location information without seeing private operational records.
roles.outcome: Arrival and orientation → accessible destination and public explanation
roles.check: Signage comprehension, public information policy and physical access

empathy.caption: Empathy map for the first-run student during the vision experiment, with the instructor and technician maps beside it. Every entry is an anticipated hypothesis from the Phase 2 record. No participant said, thought or felt these; zero participants were studied.

says: Which camera are we supposed to use?
thinks: Everyone else seems to know what they're doing.
does: Checks the brief on a phone
feels: Relieved after the first good capture
gains: Evidence that writes the report's method

others.says: Has everyone checked in? Which station is free?
others.thinks: Two kits are probably incomplete again.
others.does: Walks the room; marks attendance; fixes setups; answers repeated questions.
others.feels: Stretched across stations; frustrated by preventable delays.
others.pains: No readiness signal; manual attendance; inconsistent evidence quality.
others.gains: Readiness at a glance; attendance from check-in; rubric linked to evidence.

others.says: When did this stop working? Who had it last?
others.thinks: Who else booked this kit this week?
others.does: Tests the device; searches for accessories; updates a log; tells faculty.
others.feels: Interrupted; responsible for problems they could not see coming.
others.pains: Symptom-free reports; unknown last user; no link from a fault to future bookings.
others.gains: Structured reports with asset ID; automatic impact on bookings; verification record.
